newsitem.title: UK: Doughty Hanson takes majority stake in Impress.
newsitem.headline: Doughty Hanson takes majority stake in Impress.

text.p: British investment group Doughty Hanson & Co said on Monday it had signed a deal to become majority shareholder at Impress Metal Packaging, a company formed from the merger of the metal packaging businesses of France's Pechiney SA SA and Germany's Schmalbach-Lubeca AG.
Doughty said the deal would create Europe's second-largest food and general line metal packaging company. It said the merged group had sales of around two billion marks last year.
in a venture that also brings in Doughty Hanson & Co of Britain.
The merger, provisionally agreed last November, will go ahead at the beginning of May subject to regulatory approval, Pechiney said in a statement.
The merged business will have turnover above seven billion francs from 35 factories spread across 12 countries, it said.
Doughty, a privately-owned fund manager, said the copmany would be based in the Netherlands. The group will employ almost 8,000 staff and operate 35 manufacturing sites in 12 countries.
Doughty said Pechiney and Schmalbach, a subsidiary of German industrial group Viag AG, would each hold 20 percent of Impress.
Doughty said Dominique Damon, formerly a senior executive at Alusuisse-Lonza Holding AG and Rhone-Poulenc SA would be apointed chief executive officer at Impress.
